newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk shares ease after testing new resistance.
newsitem.headline: Turk shares ease after testing new resistance.

text.p: Istanbul shares retreated in profit-taking on Friday after testing fresh resistance at the index's 1,700 level after the recent strong gains, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed down six points, or 0.36 percent at 1,669 after brushing a high of 1,700 in early trade. Volume dropped to 27.31 trillion lira from Thursday's 37.91 trillion which included a 5.7 trillion lira block deal.
"The market struggled to keep the index at around the 1,670 level after unsuccessfully testing the 1,700 barrier in the morning," said Erdal Osanmaz from Ar securities.
"To test the 1,700 mark again, there is need for stronger volume and activity in bluechips having major effect on the market index," he added.
The 1,700 mark is the index's all-time high close set on January 27. The 1997 intra-day high was 1,751 in January.

Over the week, the index jumped 4.6 percent as the market disregarded the possibility of early polls to be held by end-1997. It had surged 8.7 percent last week on hopes of an alternative alliance to replace the ailing Islamist-led coalition.
Under Turkish law parliament must set the polling date with a majority vote. The Islamist-conservative coalition has 274 seats in the 550-member parliament, with two seats vacant.

Of the 243 shares traded, rises outdid falls by 108 to 69 and 66 ended stable. The IMKB Industrial edged up 0.19 percent to 1,555, the IMKB Services eased 0.48 percent to 1,647 and the IMKB Financial dropped 0.71 percent to 1,825.

Leading actives were largely state owned oil refiner Tupras, up 5,000 lira at 78,000, utility Cukurova Elektrik, steady at 227,500 lira and commercial vehicle venture Anadolu Isuzu, down 3,000 lira at 87,000.
They made up 20.5 percent of the total volume.
